buttons.name: Access

buttons.name: Scale Selection
buttons.desc: Resize an element using a scaling factor you specify.

buttons.name: Rotate Selection

buttons.name: Array
buttons.desc: Make multiple copies of an element, and place them in a grid formation near the original element.

buttons.name: Mirror
buttons.desc: Mirror the selection across the benchmark.

buttons.desc: Set the Z height to zero for all or all selected.

buttons.desc: Connects sprinklers to branch lines using arm-overs, sprigs and/or drops.

buttons.desc: Connects two selected pipes together using a swing joint.

buttons.desc: Connects selected pipes to each other using swing joints.

buttons.desc: Creates branch lines based on sprinkler concentrations.

buttons.desc: Sizes branch lines, outriggers, and riser nipples according to pipe sizing settings and reference.

buttons.name: Arm-Around
buttons.desc: Creates an "arm" around an obstruction according to user selected options in order to correct an intersection that causes a conflict.

buttons.name: Access
buttons.desc: View: Tool Bars: Camera Rotator

buttons.name: Hold Altitude
buttons.desc: When active, keeps camera at the same Z elevation while it moves, regardless of the direction in which it is pointed. (Note: This command is only available if you are in First Person mode.)

buttons.name: Auto Clip
buttons.desc: When active, both foreground and backdrop clipping planes are recalculated whenever the camera is moved in order to keep the entire drawing visible.

buttons.name: First Person
buttons.desc: When active, the view is shown in first-person perspective, as if you are inside the drawing at the location of the camera. Objects are rendered so as to appear three-dimensional and give the appearance of depth.

buttons.name: Increase Camera Velocity
buttons.desc: Starts camera moving forward; each click of this button increases forward velocity. Also usable to slow down backward camera motion. (Note: This command is only available if you are in First Person mode.)

buttons.name: Decrease Camera Velocity
buttons.desc: Starts camera moving backward; each click of this button increases backward velocity. Also usable to slow down forward camera motion. (Note: This command is only available if you are in First Person mode.)

buttons.name: Stop Camera Movement
buttons.desc: If the camera is moving, this stops its motion completely. (Note: This command is only available if you are in First Person mode.)

buttons.name: Move Camera Forward
buttons.desc: Moves the camera forward one movement increment. (Note: This command is only available if you are in First Person mode.)

buttons.name: Move Foreground Clip Farther
buttons.desc: Increases distance between the camera and the foreground clipping plane, the place in the foreground at which objects become visible.

buttons.name: Move Backdrop Clip Farther
buttons.desc: Increases distance between the camera and the backdrop clipping plane (also known as the background clipping plane), the place in the background beyond which objects are no longer visible.

buttons.name: Move Camera Backward
buttons.desc: Moves the camera backward one movement increment. (Note: This command is only available if you are in First Person mode.)

buttons.name: Move Foreground Clip Nearer
buttons.desc: Decreases distance between the camera and the place in the foreground at which objects become visible.

buttons.name: Move Backdrop Clip Nearer
buttons.desc: Decreases distance between the camera and the place in the background beyond which objects are no longer visible.

buttons.name: Set Camera Position
buttons.desc: Lets you set camera position and direction by clicking in the drawing.

buttons.name: Camera Position Settings
buttons.desc: Lets you set camera position and direction by entering coordinates.

buttons.name: Window Clipping Plane
buttons.desc: Equips cursor with a rectangle tool, allowing you to select an area of your drawing outside of which everything will be invisible.

buttons.desc: Allows you to draw a vertical clipping plane between two points you specify.

buttons.name: 3-Point
buttons.desc: Allows you to draw a clipping plane specified by three points.

buttons.desc: Creates a horizontal clipping plane that clips all elements above it.

buttons.desc: Creates a horizontal clipping plane that clips all elements below it.

buttons.desc: Creates a vertical clipping plane that clips all elements to its east.

buttons.desc: Creates a vertical clipping plane that clips all elements to its north.

buttons.desc: Creates a vertical clipping plane that clips all elements to its south.

buttons.desc: When an element area is selected in a drawing, this tool clips everything except the selected area.

buttons.desc: Equips the cursor with the circle tool. Draws a circle defined by three points.

buttons.name: Crosshatch
buttons.desc: Equips the cursor with the crosshatch tool. Draws a crosshatch defined by several points.

buttons.desc: Equips the cursor to place a column in the drawing.

buttons.desc: Equips the cursor to add a column line to the drawing.

buttons.name: Cloud
buttons.desc: Equips the cursor with the cloud tool. Draws a cloud defined by several points.

buttons.name: Click and Drag
buttons.desc: Several distinct views are available by selecting the appropriate toolbar icon, clicking the left mouse button, then dragging the mouse over the area in the drawing. To end a Dynamic Camera view, right-mouse click anywhere in the drawing.

buttons.desc: Removes all hydraulic node tags from the drawing.

buttons.desc: Stretches hangers that are selected in the drawing.

buttons.desc: Automatically places fittings at all pipe intersections that do no have a fitting.

buttons.desc: Breaks pipes that are too long and places couplings.

buttons.desc: Creates roof planes by connecting all selected walls and/or columns.

buttons.desc: Automatically places hangers on pipes selected in the drawing.

buttons.name: Access

buttons.name: Elbow
buttons.desc: Used to connect two pipes at a 90-degree angle.

buttons.name: Tee
buttons.desc: Used at a three-pipe intersection to connect pipes.

buttons.name: Cross
buttons.desc: Used at a four-pipe intersection to connect pipes.

buttons.name: Bushing
buttons.desc: Used to connect pipes (or pipes and fittings) of disparate sizes.

buttons.name: Cap
buttons.desc: Used at an unconnected pipe end to keep water in the pipe.

buttons.name: Coupling
buttons.desc: Used to connect two pipes end-to-end.

buttons.name: Flange
buttons.desc: Used for connections where stiff, inflexible unions are required (typically in places where high pressure is involved).

buttons.name: Valve
buttons.desc: Used to control flow of water through the pipe to which it is attached.

buttons.name: Reducer/Adapter
buttons.desc: A non-grooved fitting that does not fall into any of the other fitting categories.

buttons.name: Union
buttons.desc: A flexible fitting for rigid pipes. If two fixed pipes must be joined, a union can rotate both ways to join the pipes before being locked into position.

buttons.name: Flex Head
buttons.desc: A flexible pipe with a female connection at one end and a male connection at the other.

buttons.desc: If the camera is moving, this stops its motion completely. (Note: This command is only available if you are in First Person mode.)

buttons.name: Control Area
buttons.desc: Places a control area in the drawing.

buttons.name: Control Area Navigation Dialog
buttons.desc: Opens the Control Area Navigation dialog.

buttons.name: Access
buttons.desc: View: Tool Bars: View Rotator

buttons.name: Roll Camera Counterclockwise
buttons.desc: Rolls the camera to the left.

buttons.name: Pitch Camera Up
buttons.desc: Pitches the camera up.

buttons.name: Roll Camera Clockwise
buttons.desc: Rolls the camera to the right.

buttons.name: Yaw Camera Left
buttons.desc: Rotates the camera to the left around its own Z-axis, along the plane of its own Y-axis.

buttons.name: Move Camera to Benchmark
buttons.desc: In normal mode, points the camera at the benchmark so that the benchmark is in the center of the view. In First Person mode, moves the camera to the current location of the benchmark.

buttons.name: Yaw Camera Right
buttons.desc: Yaws the camera to the right.

buttons.name: Rotate Camera Left
buttons.desc: Rotates the camera to the left (counterclockwise).

buttons.name: Pitch Camera Down
buttons.desc: Pitches the camera down.

buttons.name: Rotate Camera Right
buttons.desc: Rotates the camera to the right (clockwise).

buttons.name: Left Side View
buttons.desc: Sets the view to the left edge of your drawing.

buttons.name: Front View
buttons.desc: Sets the view to the "front" edge of your drawing.

buttons.name: Right Side View
buttons.desc: Sets the view to the right edge of your drawing.

buttons.name: Back View
buttons.desc: Sets the view to the "back" edge of your drawing.

buttons.name: Zoom Camera to Area
buttons.desc: Zooms in on an area you select so that area fills the drawing window.

buttons.name: Zoom All
buttons.desc: Changes zoom level so all elements in the drawing are visible in the drawing window.

buttons.name: Zoom In
buttons.desc: Zooms in one zoom increment. (Hold down the <Shift> key for a smaller zoom increment.)

buttons.name: Zoom Out
buttons.desc: Zooms out one zoom increment. (Hold down the <Shift> key for a smaller zoom increment.)

buttons.name: Previous Camera Position
buttons.desc: Restores the view to the camera position immediately preceding the current camera position.

buttons.name: Isometric View
buttons.desc: Sets the view to above your drawing and towards its southwest corner. All three drawing axes are scaled equally.

buttons.name: Top View
buttons.desc: Sets the view to directly above your drawing, with the view direction parallel to the Z-axis of the drawing. (This is also known as plan view.)

buttons.name: Next Camera Position
buttons.desc: Restores the view to the camera position immediately after the current camera position. (Note: This button is not available unless the Previous Camera Position button has been used.)
